title: question-probes/1
description: The sub-questions of tables' open questions, one item each, and for every sub-question the data can answer one SELECT a person runs on the platform. The tool never runs it. `semantic probes check` holds the file to its checks; whether an item's class, query and target fit together is the checks' to say, not this schema's.

placeholders.description: Each placeholder the queries use (`${name}`) with an example value: the check puts it in before parsing, the person running a query puts the real one.

id.description: The item's id, unique in the file; an observation's `query` names it.

table.description: The table the question is about (db.table).

question.description: The question's id in the table's document.

asked.description: The question's text as the document asked it when the item was written.

part.description: The sub-question's number within the question, from 1.

class.description: Who can answer: `data` (a query), `human` (a person), `corpus` (the task SQL or the documents already say).

shape.description: What the query finds: `uniqueness` and `value_set` have fixed output columns and may land in an observation slot; any other word (such as `conditional_count`) is evidence for an answer only.

sql.description: One SELECT, Spark SQL, placeholders as `${name}`.

partitions.description: The partitions the query reads: one item per partitioned table, the value wanted and what to do when that partition is not there yet.

full_scan.description: Why the query reads a partitioned table without a partition filter; null or absent when it does not.

engine.description: The engine to run the query on (such as `spark`).

lands.description: The observation target the result may become, or null: `summary.row.observed`, `column:<c>.observed_values` or `input:<db.table>`.

how_to_read.description: How to read the result to answer the sub-question.

note.description: For a `human` or `corpus` item: who or what answers it, and how.
